question: Recent media reports1 have highlighted cases of alleged deliberate abuse and injury of dogs in Uganda, with videos of their suffering shared on social media to solicit donations.

While the alleged perpetrators have reportedly been arrested, concerns have also been raised that some of the confiscated animals have subsequently been euthanised due to insufficient shelter capacity, veterinary care and financial resources. Animal welfare is closely linked to public health, sustainable development, food security and the One Health approach.

Article 13 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union recognises animals as sentient beings and requires the EU to pay full regard to animal welfare requirements in the formulation and implementation of its policies. 1.
Is the Commission aware of these reports and has it raised these concerns with the Ugandan authorities?

Does the Commission support, directly or indirectly, projects in Uganda that strengthen animal welfare protection, including through veterinary services, shelter capacity, humane dog population management and the enforcement of animal welfare legislation?

Will the Commission consider further integrating animal welfare into its development cooperation with Uganda, including by strengthening the capacity of the competent authorities and civil society organisations to rescue, rehabilitate and protect animals that are subjected to cruelty?
